narr: A slow moving cold front, located near the Arkansas and Missouri borders, set the stage for a dangerous flood event to unfold on the night of the 16th into the morning of the 17th across north-central into central portions of Arkansas. Rainfall amounts of 4 to 9 inches were measured. This much rain in a relatively short amount of time lead to flash flooding, some of which was significant.
ev: Multiple roads flooded in southern Conway as a result of high water via Stone Dan Creek overflowing out of its banks.
East of the town of Marshall, parts of Arkansas Highway 74E were covered by high water along with several county roads that were washed out in northeastern Searcy county.
In the town of Heber Springs, multiple roads were impassable and a few roads were completely washed out across parts of Heber Springs and county roads within Cleburne County.
In the city of Conway, water was over the roadway at the intersection of Sugar Creek Drive and Donaghey Avenue.
In the vicinity of Mountain View, the area of Round Bottom Road and Herpel Road was flooded and was evacuated due to rising water.
High, fast moving water flowed over the Arkansas Highway 14 bridge over Town Branch which is a tributary of Crooked Creek in Yellville.
The Marion County Road 8060 bridge over Moccasin Creek was partially washed out and impassable from flash flooding and high water over the bridge near Fairview.
Flash flooding covered roads and exceeded ditches in the towns of Annieville and Imboden.
In the community of Conway street flooding took place in downtown with a car becoming stranded in the water over the roadway.
In Yellville, the Marion County courthouse was flooded. In the vicinity of Flippin, several residents were evacuated due to water enter homes.
Multiple homes along Dee Lane, just east of the city of Conway were flooded. Additionally, multiple roads were flooded throughout the county.
Flash Flooding occurred along Machine Creek in the community of Smithville.
Creekside Nursing Home/Rehabilitation Center was evacuated due to water that was rising to a height as high as the bed sides of many residents.
Portions of Arkansas Highway 287 between the towns of Plumerville and Morrilton impassible due to water completely covering the roadway.
Multiple county roads were impassable and some county roads were washed out in northwestern Stone County.
An apartment complex off of Mountain Drive was flooding on Mountain Drive in the town of Greenbrier.
